Rhetoric has come to mean pompous. Which is completely wrong. Rhetoric is Aristotle's discussion of how to deliver information to people. The five cannons of the field of rhetoric are: invention, arrangement, style, memory, and delivery.

The way you speak is wonderful. Your audience is not. Your audience is on a similar bell curve as all of the rest of humanity as it applies to how they communicate. From the eloquent to the inarticulate, there is an unknowable average. However, your issue is not with how articulate you are. It is how your audience receives information that may be the stumbling block here.
If so, the Rhetoric cannons 3 and 5 (arrangement and delivery) might be of some use. A person whose learning style is visual and not auditory might just be expressing frustration. They here some one well spoken, but their learning style does not match your teaching style. 

The cannon of arrangement charges us with the duty of understanding our audience. Understand that they might be just as confused as your are as to why they are not understanding the information you are providing. A visual learner needs pictures. Which you are in no way required to provide, nor am I encouraging you to change what you are doing. But I have heard your complaints on several occasions, and I am hoping this might help bring some clarity.
